Those Who Remain — teardown

COMBAT-PROGRESSION · Peak Development Studios · placeId 488667523 · Shooter / PvE Shooter · co-op 8p

Co-op round survival against waves of the infected: shoot to survive, and survive to earn what you survive with next. Up to 8 players per server hold off escalating infected waves on maps (Ranch / District / Skyscraper). Kills pay Credits (even passively, from teammates' kills); between waves, in the intermission, you open Loadout / Perks / Shop and buy weapons (gated by level and price), perks and cosmetics. Weapons are real firearms, unlocked by level (1->64) and priced in Credits (€4,100->€455,000), buyable early at a premium. Modes: Play / Endless / Classic / Hardcore. The player's own formula: "you survive to earn money, you earn money to survive better."

01Classification

The repeated action is survive: gun down waves of the infected in co-op, bank Credits from kills and levels, and unlock/buy weapons and perks to hold out in harder waves.

Verb
Survive - hold off escalating waves of the infected in co-op (up to 8 players), sticking with the team and completing objectives (Survival / Escort / Survive until minute N).
Theme
Co-op zombie survival: several infected types, maps (Ranch / District / Skyscraper), real firearms, a Credits economy, level gating. "One of Roblox's original zombie-survival experiences" (created 2016).
Systems
Combat · Wave Defense · Inventory and Equipment · Upgrade Tree (perks) · Container Gacha (skin cases) · Daily Rewards · Quests (wave objectives) · Collection (weapons/skins).
Economy
Credits (€) - the in-game currency from kills (and passively from teammates' kills); spent on weapons, perks, skins, power-ups. XP is a separate axis that unlocks weapons/perks by level. Robux buys Credit packs, power-ups, gamepasses. No item selling.
Pre-class delta
Description-only pre-classification returned MANAGER-TYCOON (wrong). RADAR labelled it 'VS Zombies Survival' (sim 0.83), closer. Play confirmed COMBAT-PROGRESSION: combat -> Credits+level -> stronger weapons -> survive hard waves.
Mask
Under a survival label it is a co-op wave-shooter with a dual progression gate: weapons unlock by level AND cost Credits (or are bought early at a premium). Cosmetics (skins) are colors only, pure cosmetic-only. The core loop is survive<->earn, as the player himself frames it.
[COMBAT-PROGRESSION: fight→earn→arm→survive] + combat + wave-defense + inventory-equipment + upgrade-tree + container-gacha + daily-rewards + quests + guidance-rail | {co-op-zombie-wave-survival-shooter · round-based · cooperative} × power-ladder - the match is round-based (waves + intermission) and cooperative (up to 8p; teammates' kills pay you); progress follows a power-ladder (level+Credits unlock weapons/perks), waves follow a wave-ladder, and skins are a cosmetic-only container-gacha $ wall:level-and-credit-gates→offer:credit-packs-and-gamepasses ! combat-impact-ceremony

The recording centers on one dense session. Joined via the Server List, the game dropped straight into Endless already on wave 8 (open world, many players). The author holds off, reaches the intermission, tours every menu (Loadout / Perks / Shop / Spectate / Options / Leaderboards), then a map vote, a fresh match from wave 5 to 6. 03Menu & modes

Entry is via the Server List: modes Play / Endless / Classic / Hardcore, public 8-player servers labelled with map and fill. No tutorial - straight into the fight.

The menu is spare and tutorial-free. The entry point is the Server List: 8-player public servers, each with its own mode (Play, Endless, Classic, Hardcore) and map (Ranch, District, Skyscraper, Expressway). You can make a private server (or buy Permanent Private Servers for Robux). Joining can drop you straight into the server's current wave - as in the recording, where the start was wave 8 of Endless. The "first screen" role is played by the Daily Rewards panel with a rising payout ladder and multiplier days - the first return hook before any combat.

04Core loop: waves & intermission

A match alternates two phases: the wave (hold off, bank Credits and XP, complete objectives) and the intermission (open Loadout / Perks / Shop, buy and equip). Between maps there is a vote; within, a skip-to-wave vote.

The match's core loop is two beats. The wave: stick with the team, gun down the infected, and each kill drips Credits and XP into the kill feed, while objectives (Survival / Escort the VIP / Survive until minute N / Repair the track) pay a bonus (+1,000 Credits and XP). The intermission: between waves a menu opens - Loadout (swap/buy weapons), Perks, Shop, Spectate (watch players, gift spawn tokens) - where you sink your earnings into power. The party votes on a map before a match and can skip early waves (Skip to Wave). The author nails the essence: "you survive to earn money, you earn money to survive better."

05Infected & kill economy

The infected come in several types with rising kill value: from Civilian (+10) to Bloater (+100). Headshots and assists add a bonus. This is the income source - the economy hangs directly on kills.

InfectedKill (Credits)Headshot bonusNote
Civilian+10+5basic, most common
Sprinter+10+5fast, chases you down
Military+25+13tougher
Burster+50+25leaves a damage cloud on death
Hazmat+75+30dangerous, lots of HP
Bloater+100+50highest-value kill (observed +100)
Riot · Bolter · Juggernautspecial-shown in kill stats; special types
Assist+25+13for helping down an enemy

The game's economy literally hangs on kills: the kill feed pays Credits for every infected, and value scales with the type's danger - Civilian/Sprinter +10, Military +25, Burster +50, Hazmat +75, Bloater +100, plus a headshot bonus (about +50%) and an assist (+25). Types differ in behavior: the Sprinter chases you down, the Burster drops a damage cloud on death, Hazmat/Bloater are "tanky" targets. Stats also track special types (Riot, Bolter, Juggernaut) and special kills (Headshot, Decapitation, Long Range, Explosive, Fire, Barbed Wire). The key co-op nuance: Credits drip even passively - from infected your teammates kill - so staying near the team pays off both in money and in survival.

Every weapon, when selected, shows a full 7-stat card: Damage · Bullet Punch · Fire Rate (RPM) · Recoil · Magnification · Ammo Capacity · Reload Time - so a weapon choice balances role (the Winchester sniper 100 dmg/7x vs the high-rate CZ Scorpion 1,100 RPM), price and level.

The Loadout is the second (and main) progression axis, laid out across Primary / Secondary / Melee / Utility tabs. The weapons are recognizable real firearms (Sawn Off, Ruger 10/22, MAC-10, Sten, Mossberg, Thompson, Benelli, TEC-9, Taurus, Obrez Mosin, Gepard PDW...), and each has a dual gate: first the required level (1->64), then a Credits price (€4,100 at the start -> €455,000 at the top). The key device is "buy early at a premium": you can grab a weapon below your level, but the early-buy price is far higher (€24,440, €54,933, €806,250 in the recording) and drops as your level rises - soft pressure on grind/spend without a hard wall. Every weapon carries honest stats (damage, fire rate, recoil, magnification, ammo capacity, reload), so the choice is a balance of role and price.

07Perks

Perks are three trees (Survivalist / Craftsman / Marksman) with nodes at levels 10 -> 100. Slots are few (3 in the recording); more open by level and the Extra Perk gamepass. Passive survival and damage boosts.

Perks are the third layer of power and meta. They are laid out across three trees - Survivalist, Craftsman, Marksman - and each tree's nodes open at level milestones 10 -> 20 -> 30 -> 45 -> 60 -> 85 -> 100 (effects like "reduces the effect of X by 50%"). The limiter is the slot count: the recording shows 3 available, more open as your level rises, and one more comes from the Extra Perk gamepass (450 R$). So perks are tied both to progress (level) and to monetization (a slot for Robux), while staying passive boosts rather than active abilities.

08Shop: skins & power-ups

The shop has three tabs: Credits (packs for Robux), Power-Ups/Passes (boosts + gamepasses) and Skins - tiered gacha cases with a flat chance. Crucially: skins are colors only, pure cosmetic.

The shop splits into three tabs. Credits - packs of the in-game currency for Robux with a wholesale bonus (+30% / +45% on the big ones). Power-Ups / Passes - consumable boosts (Credit Boost x2, Exp Boost x2 for 20 wave minutes, spawn tokens, bandoliers) and permanent gamepasses. Skins - six gacha cases (Tier I/II/III - ¢6,000 / ¢20,000 / ¢50,000, and Tactical/Neon/Ethereal - ¢12,000 / ¢120,000 / ¢1,000,000) with a flat chance per item (Tier I - 5.00%, Tier II - 5.26%). The key, healthy design point: case contents are colors/patterns only, cosmetics do not affect power, so the gacha here is a Credits sink rather than pay-to-win.

09Economy & formulas

Numbers read off in-game screens, distilled into rules. Two progression axes - Credits (spend) and XP/level (gate), plus a daily ladder. No passive currency except kill income (including teammates' kills).

Kill rewards (Credits)

TypeKillHeadshotAssist
Civilian / Sprinter+10+5+25 / +13
Military+25+13-
Burster+50+25-
Hazmat+75+30-
Bloater+100+50-

Level XP curve (EXP to next)

Level (observed)EXP to nextWhat it unlocks
early3,000first guns (lvl 1-13)
mid3,600 -> 4,225 -> 4,900weapons lvl 14-17, perk slots (10/20)
later5,625 -> 6,400 -> 7,225 -> 8,100weapons lvl 18+, perk trees 30->100

The economy rests on two axes. Credits (€) - the spend: banked from kills (see table), wave objectives (+1,000) and the daily ladder ($3,000 -> $10,000 + multiplier days), spent on weapons, perks, skins and power-ups; the balance in the recording swung 2,000 -> 23,766 -> 47,359. XP/level - the gate: XP-to-next rises (~3,000 -> 8,100), and every level opens new weapons and perk slots/nodes. A separate formula is "buy a weapon before its level": the early-buy premium is far above the base price and falls as your level rises (€24,440 / €54,933 / €806,250 in the recording). There is no passive income - except income from kills, including teammates' (from infected your teammates kill).

10Monetization

Respectful monetization: power is not sold directly (skins are colors only). Robux buys acceleration (Credit packs, boosts) and convenience/cosmetics (8 gamepasses). Plus donations.

GroupItemsPrice, Robux
Credit packs€3,000 · €9,675 · €34,500 · €75,000 · €156,000(+30%) · €478,500(+45%)50 · 150 · 500 · 1,000 · 2,000 · 5,500
Power-upsSpawn In Token (x1/x10) · Bandolier (x1/x10)25 / 200 · 20 / 160
BoostsCredit Boost x2 · Exp Boost x2 (20 min)65 · 80
Gamepass - conveniencePermanent Private Servers · Extra Perk · Freecam600 · 450 · 800
Gamepass - cosmeticColored Tracers · Rainbow Chat · Custom Tag · Custom Death Sound500 · 400 · 200 · 350
DonationsDonation · Gold Gift · Excessive Donation250 · 1,500 · 2,500

Monetization is built on acceleration and convenience, not on selling power directly. Robux buys: Credit packs (50->5,500 R$ for €3,000->€478,500, with a wholesale bonus), consumable boosts (Credit/Exp Boost x2, spawn tokens, bandoliers) and 8 gamepasses, which split into convenience (Permanent Private Servers, Extra Perk - +slot, Freecam) and cosmetics (Colored Tracers, Rainbow Chat, Custom Tag, Custom Death Sound). Plus explicit donations (Donation / Gold Gift / Excessive Donation). Skin cases, meanwhile, are bought only with in-game Credits and give colors only - so even the gacha layer is not pay-to-win. It is a "soft" model: the payer saves time and gets convenience, but no combat advantage.

11Co-op & pickups

The game is built for a team: near players you barely die, and teammates' kills pay you Credits. Maps are scattered with pickups (grenades, ammo, armor, medkits, barbed wire - which you can place).

Co-op is not an option but a load-bearing mechanic. The author says outright: "it's very hard to die, especially if you stay near players," and Credits drip from teammates' kills, so the team pays off twice over. Maps are scattered with pickups grabbed on E: armor (blue refreshes defense), medkits, ammo, grenades (take in hand -> throw -> blast) and barbed wire, which you place with a hammer/tool (a BARBED WIRE counter at the bottom) - the one bit of "building/defense"; there are also Repair objectives ("Repair the track"). The social layer: Spectate dead players, gifting spawn-in tokens and visible teammate levels (players at 122-143 lvl in the recording - a sign of long grinding). All of it pulls you to form a group and return together.

12HUD & menus

In combat the HUD is dense but diegetic: HP and armor gauges bottom-right, the kill feed top-right (Credits+XP per kill), objectives left, an XP bar at the bottom, wave counter and timer up top. 30 marked UI screens.

The interface splits by mode. In combat the HUD is dense but readable: circular HP and armor gauges bottom-right, the kill feed top-right awarding Credits/XP per kill, objectives (Survival / Escort / Survive until minute N) left, an XP bar at the bottom, the wave counter and timer up top, plus the party ready list in the intermission. In menus everything moves to a left column of tabs (Loadout / Perks / Shop / Spectate / Options / Leaderboards) on one "tabs -> content -> action" layout. The 30 marked UI screens are mostly states of these stable panels plus the wave<->intermission transition and votes (map, skip-to-wave).

13Retention

Hooks: a daily ladder, a weekly leaderboard with a seasonal reset, a long level grind (weapons/perks to 100), several modes and special-kill tracking. Plus co-op itself pulls you back with a team.

Retention spans several horizons. Short - the match itself (further wave, more kills and Credits) plus the daily ladder with multiplier days. Medium - the weekly leaderboard with a seasonal reset (leaders at 100K+ kills) and special-kill tracking, a competitive goal. Long - a level grind to 100: weapons and perk nodes open by level (players at 122-143 lvl in the recording - dozens of hours), plus a weapon and skin collection and several modes (Endless / Classic / Hardcore). Co-op itself retains: near a team, surviving is easier and more profitable, so the game pulls you to gather a group and return.

14Badges

The game has no official Roblox badges - progress and status rest on internal systems (level, the weekly leaderboard, special-kill tracking) rather than a badge funnel.

Unlike many games in the pool, Those Who Remain does not use official Roblox badges as a progression axis - its badge catalog is empty. All the "checklist and status" work is carried by internal systems: level (unlocks weapons/perks, shown above a player as an icon), the weekly leaderboard with a seasonal reset, and personal stats (kills by infected type and special kills - Headshot / Decapitation / Long Range / Explosive / Fire / Barbed Wire). It is a deliberate choice: progress is measured by level and kills inside the game, not by external marks.

Feedback works on combat weight - a combat-impact-ceremony: the author calls the game "pretty juicy." Weapons land a dense transient, the kill feed gives a numeric response, HP/armor gauges are diegetic. Data is from short combat clips.

Feedback is grounded in combat weight - a combat-impact-ceremony, and the author himself calls the game "pretty juicy." Weapons answer with a dense shot transient and an enemy reaction, and the kill feed instantly gives a numeric response (Credits/XP) that differs by infected type - so sound and numbers report the kill's value. Isolated game-audio measurements hold in a tight combat band (-13...-17 dB), peaking on the early wave theme. Diegetics - circular HP/armor gauges in the corner. The one weak spot the author flags: hit registration is sometimes late. The portable lesson: keep the combat response and the numeric reward in one frame (shot -> reaction -> +Credits in the feed), and tie the weight of the sound to the target type.

18What to take

Decisions that make a co-op wave-shooter sticky and monetized respectfully - without pay-to-win in combat.

1

Close the survive-earn loop

Credits drip from kills and are spent on weapons/perks for survival. The survive<->earn loop is self-evident and holds the match: "you survive to earn money, you earn money to survive."

2

Hang the economy on enemy type

Kill value scales with danger (Civilian +10 -> Bloater +100) + a headshot bonus. The player naturally reaches for hard targets - risk-reward is baked into the shooting.

3

Dual-gate the weapons

Weapons unlock by LEVEL and cost Credits. Level gives a long progression, price a constant spend goal; together, a deep leveled storefront (1->64).

4

"Buy early at a premium"

You can grab a weapon below your level, but pricier, and the price falls with level. Soft pressure on grind/spend without a hard wall - and a hook for Robux Credit packs.

5

Make co-op pay

Near players you don't die, and teammates' kills pay you. The mechanic directly rewards sticking with a team - both retention and a social hook.

6

Keep cosmetics out of power

Skin cases are colors only and bought with in-game Credits. Even the gacha layer is not pay-to-win; power is not sold directly - which defuses anti-p2w critique.

7

Monetize convenience, not damage

Robux buys Credit packs, boosts (Credit/Exp x2), private servers, an extra perk slot and cosmetics. The payer saves time and gets convenience, not an edge.

8

Diegetic combat status

HP and armor are circular gauges in the corner, and the kill feed shows the reward instantly. Status reads in the combat frame, without a heavy text overlay.

9

Retain on level and leaderboard

A daily ladder, a weekly leaderboard with a seasonal reset, a grind to 100 and special-kill tracking give hooks across every horizon without a skin daily-calendar.
